# RaftKV v1.0.0

The first release: a small replicated key-value store you can **watch think**. Three
processes elect a leader, agree on every write, survive `kill -9`, and serve a key-value
API with linearizable reads, while a live dashboard shows elections and replication as
they happen. Stop the leader and watch the cluster elect a new one in about half a second.

## Highlights

- **Real Raft, real processes.** Built on [RaftCore](https://github.com/privateMwb/RaftCore):
  randomized election timeouts, log replication, majority commit.
- **Durable.** Every append is `fsync`ed to a write-ahead log before it is acknowledged; a
  node killed with `SIGKILL` restarts from disk and catches up.
- **Honest reads.** Linearizable by default. Without a quorum you get a `503`, never a stale
  answer. `?stale=1` opts into a node's local copy.
- **A dashboard that tells the truth.** It listens to every node, so a cut-off old leader is
  shown alive and marked *stale* rather than mistaken for dead.
- **Break it on purpose.** Kill, Revive, Isolate, and a delay slider act on the real
  cluster. Works on a phone too.
- **Ready to host.** A single-port gateway, a demo image, and a Render blueprint put the
  whole cluster behind one URL, with the dashboard on Vercel. See
  [docs/DEPLOYMENT.md](docs/DEPLOYMENT.md).

## What's included

### Backend (C++23)

- Client API on each node's one HTTP port: `PUT`/`GET`/`DELETE /kv/<key>`, `307` redirects
  from followers to the leader, rate limiting (default 600 requests per client per 10 s),
  and a 64 KiB value cap.
- Live state over Server-Sent Events: `/events`, `/cluster/events`, `/status`, `/cluster`.
- A stdin REPL and a headless mode, plus a test suite (`./build/raftkv_tests`) that includes
  real multi-node election, failover, and replication scenarios.

### Launcher and dashboard

- `scripts/launcher.mjs` runs a local three-node cluster and injects faults through
  node-to-node proxies: `SIGKILL`, per-link delay, isolation, and partitions.
- React 19 + Vite + Tailwind CSS v4 dashboard with a derived event feed, plain-language
  narration, and a key-value console.

### Hosted demo

- `scripts/gateway.mjs` serves the cluster on one port: an allowlist of routes (never the
  nodes' peer-to-peer RPC), CORS for configured origins only, rate limits, and one shared
  live stream per node so any number of visitors cost a node one connection.
- A watchdog heals a cluster that visitors leave broken; `Dockerfile.demo`, `render.yaml`,
  and `frontend/vercel.json` deploy it; `scripts/check-demo.sh` verifies a running demo.

### Docs and tooling

- [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) and a ten-minute [guided demo](docs/DEMO.md).
- CI: Build (GCC and Clang, Debug and Release) runs the full test suite; Sanitizers runs it
  again under ASan/UBSan and under TSan, plus a real-node smoke test; Clang Format, Clang
  Tidy, CodeQL, Frontend, Docs, Release; Dependabot for Actions and npm.
- [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md), [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md), and a
  [CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md).

## Try it

```bash
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/privateMwb/RaftKV
cd RaftKV/backend
cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build
cd ..

npm --prefix frontend install
node scripts/launcher.mjs --fresh      # 3 nodes + the kill/revive launcher
npm --prefix frontend run dev          # http://localhost:5173
```

Requires a C++23 compiler, CMake 3.20+, and Node.js 22+.

## Known limitations

- **Not for production.** There is no authentication or TLS, and the launcher's
  `--host 0.0.0.0` exposes node-killing controls to your network. See
  [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).
- **The hosted-demo deployment is untested on Render and Vercel.** The gateway and the
  dashboard's client logic were tested locally against the real backend, and CI builds and
  checks the demo image, but nothing has been deployed yet.
- **Docker is untested.** The compose file parses and the argument lists are accepted by
  the real binary, but it has never been run in a container runtime.
- **No snapshots or log compaction**, and **no membership changes**: the cluster is the
  static `--peer` list.
- Peer addresses must be dotted IPv4.
- A write that times out may still commit, and there is no request deduplication.
- Under high network delay (about 80 ms one-way and up) writes fail with `503` while the
  cluster re-elects. Safety holds; only availability suffers.

Full details: [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md#known-limits).
